name: Bhunjia
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.note: Only Grierson LSI 1905 wordlist (4pp) exists per Glottolog; no phonology/grammar of Bhunjia found

sources.note: Bhunjia appears only in a tribal-language inventory table (Ota & Patel 2021, Indo-Aryan group: '.. Baiga, Bhunjia, Halbi') and in SCSTRTI publication lists; no linguistic content.

sources.citation: Ota, A. B. & S. C. Mohanty. 2020. Bhunjia (Photo Handbook). Bhubaneswar: SCSTRTI.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing; ethnographic handbook; language described only as 'a dialect of Hindi which resembles the dialect of the Halbas' / 'corrupt form of Odia'.

sources.citation: Odia-Bhunjia Sabdakosh [Odia-Bhunjia dictionary]. 2018. Special Development Council / Planning & Convergence Dept., Govt. of Odisha (SCSTRTI series).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Bilingual word list in Odia script; archive.org scanned of the Odia script is unusable; no grammar/phonology section evident. Not usable for stress.

sources.citation: Abidi, Shammi, Anil Virulkar, Mohan Sahu, Amar Das & Bhooshan Singh Netam. 2017. Bhunjiya janjati ka manavshastriya adhyayan [Anthropological study of the Bhunjiya tribe; in Hindi]. Nava Raipur: Tribal Research and Training Institute.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing; Hindi ethnographic report (origin, demography, kinship, economy, religion); a full-text search for stress/accent bhasha/boli/uchcharan/balaghat/svaraghat finds no language chapter.

sources.citation: CIIL-SPPEL (Scheme for Protection and Preservation of Endangered Languages). c.2016-2019. 'Bhunjia' project flyer (2 pp.) and 'Bhunjia Documentation' web page (the Internet Archive 2016 and live 2026).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing; people/language/culture profile of Chukutia Bhunjia of Nuapada; states a Chukutia Bhunjia-Odia-English dictionary and a Bhunjia grammar are in preparation. Bhunjia is absent from SPPEL's published grammatical-sketch list and from its WALS-style 'grammatical features' database.

sources.citation: Language Division, Office of the Registrar General, India. 2002. Linguistic Survey of India, Special Studies: Orissa. Kolkata. (incl. M. K. Koul, 'Tribal dialects of Oriya').
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Does not cover Bhunjia at all (contents: Oriya, Sambalpuri, Desia, Relli, Bhatri, Bhuyan, KeLa, Kandha/Dal/Sahara/Sabar/Gondo dialects of Oriya, Laria, Binjhia, Sadri + Munda/Dravidian); a full-text search for stress/accent bhunj = 0.

sources.citation: Patnaik, Nityananda, Prasanta Kumar Mohanty & Trilochan Sahoo. 1984. Life in Sonabera Plateau: Anthropology of the Bhunjias of Kalahandi, Orissa. Bhubaneswar: Tribal and Harijan Research-cum-Training Institute.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing; ethnography. p.3: 'The Bhunjias have no language of their own. The dialect which they speak is a mixture of Oriya and Chhatisgari.'

sources.citation: Grierson, George A. 1905. Linguistic Survey of India, vol. VII: Indo-Aryan family, Southern group: Specimens of the Marathi language. Calcutta: Office of the Superintendent of Government Printing. 'Bhunjia' pp. 372-376; Halbi 'Pronunciation' pp. 331-332.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. p.372: 'Bhunjia is closely related to Halbi. The phonetical system and the inflection of nouns is practically the same.' The Halbi 'Pronunciation' notes (pp.331-332) treat vowel interchange, anunasika, palatals, cerebrals, h; no accent statement. Silent.

sources.citation: CIIL-SPPEL (PI Sudipta Bhattacharjee). in preparation. Bhunjia grammar / ethnolinguistic profile (announced on the SPPEL Bhunjia documentation page).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: SPPEL grammatical sketches follow a template with a 'suprasegmental features' subsection; would be the first phonological description of Bhunjia if released.
